questions.q: Define situational irony and give one example from "काका साहब" where the outcome contradicts the characters' expectations.
questions.a: Situational irony occurs when actions produce an outcome opposite to what was intended or expected. In "काका साहब", the teacher expects the boy to name a conventional profession, but the boy says "I'll become a wanderer" — ironically, his wandering leads to real education while formal schooling failed him. A wrong answer (e.g., "irony is just sarcasm") reveals confusion between verbal irony (tone-based) and situational irony (outcome-based), and inability to locate textual evidence.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the spectacles (ऐनक) in "आंखों की झूठी गवाही" function as a symbol, not just a plot device.
questions.a: The spectacles symbolize specialized knowledge that gatekeeps truth — the eye specialist claims only experts can examine eyes, but the narrator argues everyone has the right to self-knowledge. They represent how institutions (medical, educational) monopolize understanding. A wrong answer (e.g., "spectacles help the old man see") treats them only as literal objects, missing the symbolic layer about epistemic authority and democratic access to knowledge.

questions.q: Apply the concept of dramatic irony to "पिंजरे की उड़ान": identify what the reader knows that the characters (the old man, the birds) do not, and how this creates tension.
questions.a: The reader knows the old man's "test" is a metaphor for life choices, while the birds (and initially the narrator) perceive it literally as a game. This creates dramatic irony — we understand the philosophical weight (freedom vs security, tradition vs modernity) before the characters do. A wrong answer (e.g., "the birds don't know they're in a cage") misses that dramatic irony requires reader's superior knowledge, not just character ignorance.

questions.q: Analyze how verbal irony operates in the narrator's tone when describing the education system in "काका साहब". Quote one phrase and explain its double meaning.
questions.a: The phrase "शिक्षा के नाम पर बच्चों पर लादी जाने वाली बोझ" (the burden imposed on children in the name of education) uses verbal irony — "शिक्षा के नाम पर" (in the name of education) superficially honors the system, while "लादी जाने वाली बोझ" (imposed burden) exposes its oppressive reality. The double meaning critiques hollow formalities. A wrong answer (e.g., "the narrator is angry") identifies emotion but not the linguistic mechanism of saying one thing to mean its opposite.

questions.q: Evaluate: Which story uses symbolism more effectively to convey its central theme — "आंखों की झूठी गवाही" (spectacles) or "पिंजरे की उड़ान" (birds)? Justify with two comparative points.
questions.a: "पिंजरे की उड़ान" uses birds more effectively because: (1) the three birds map directly onto three life philosophies (materialism, tradition, spirituality) making the symbol structurally integral, not decorative; (2) the final poem ("जन्म-मृत्यु के चक्र में...") explicitly links bird-flight to human existential cycles, creating a closed symbolic system. Spectacles in the other story are powerful but remain a single metaphor. A wrong answer (e.g., "both are equal") fails to evaluate comparative structural integration of symbol into theme.

questions.q: Create a new symbolic object for a modern retelling of "काका साहब" that represents the gap between institutional education and real learning. Describe the object and explain its symbolic layers.
questions.a: A cracked smartphone screen: literally a damaged device, symbolically representing how digital education (online classes, apps) promises access but delivers fragmented, superficial knowledge. The cracks = systemic flaws; the glowing screen = illusion of enlightenment; the touch interface = passive consumption mistaken for interaction. A poor answer (e.g., "a broken book") merely transplants the old symbol without adapting to contemporary context, showing inability to transfer symbolic thinking.
